subject: IP infringement indemnity — Order Form redlines & approval ladder
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: IP indemnity redlines on Acme order form + approval ladder

Kimberly / Jordan —

Following up on the Acme order form redlines. They circulated a fresh mark (attached) that tightens our indemnity language around third-party IP claims and narrows the customer-side obligations. I think we need:

- A short internal note confirming the acceptable carveouts for open-source obligations and downstream reseller claims.
- A recommended counter: keep the customer indemnity limited to direct claims arising from customer input (not downstream reuse), but accept a standard notice/cooperation obligation.
- A clear approval ladder so Sales knows who must sign off on any concession > $500k or any change to the defense control split.

I'm suggesting a quick huddle today so we can respond before their procurement window closes. Attaching their redlines and a draft package with our proposed replacement clause.

Attachments: [Acme_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.docx (docx)], [Redwood_Proposed_Clause_Pkg.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

---

Note: Jordan, please confirm whether ACME flagged any insurance offsets or escrow asks on the call yesterday so we can include that in the approval ladder discussion.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IP indemnity redlines on Acme order form + approval ladder

Thanks, Jasmine. Reviewed the mark briefly — high-level thoughts:

1) Cap and carveouts
- We should propose a capped exposure tied to the order form value (e.g., greater of $1M or 2x annual fees) rather than uncapped.
- Preserve an open-source carveout (OSS exceptions) and developer tooling exceptions (models trained entirely on customer data).

2) Defense & control
- Push back on unconditional right to control defense; suggest mutual cooperation and Redwood retains ability to propose counsel when technical remediation is required.

3) Third-party claims flow
- Add a short process bullet: notice → Redwood evaluates → if Redwood elects to defend, Redwood will seek full control subject to reasonable cooperation; if Redwood declines, then we propose mediation step.

4) Approval ladder (draft):
- Account Exec (Jordan): initial commercial concession approval up to $50k
- Director of Sales: approvals between $50k–$250k
- VP Sales + General Counsel (Kimberly): approvals $250k–$500k
- CEO / CFO signoff required for concessions > $500k or for any uncapped indemnity change

I'll prepare a redline (short) that: trims the customer indemnity to customer inputs, adds the OSS carveout, proposes the cap, and includes the notice/mediation flow.

I can be on a quick call 11:00am PT if that works.

-Kimberly
Senior Associate, Legal | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme.com>

Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IP infringement indemnity — Order Form redlines & approval ladder

Jasmine —

Thanks for the package and Kimberly for the quick review. A couple of points from Acme procurement / legal:

- Our leadership is sensitive to uncapped third-party IP exposure. We need any cap to be meaningful; the relationship is strategic and Acme cannot accept a 2x-fee floor that effectively leaves them exposed for a large integrated deployment.
- We are willing to accept your OSS carveout, but we need clearer language on what constitutes "customer input" — suggest narrow examples and a 30-day remediation window.
- Regarding defense control: Acme typically requires the right to control litigation once they are the claimant. If Redwood proposes counsel, we will want an approval step and the ability to substitute counsel for cause.

I realize this is commercial and legal mixed. Can we schedule a 30-minute working session Monday to walk through one tidy redline so procurement can submit to leadership on Tuesday? I've included our outside counsel (D. Harper) for any nuanced IP pushback.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-ACME-2027

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Procurement Lead, Acme Corporation
samantha.ortiz@acme.com
